feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence: iterations 0 to 4 show max_error pinned at 0.0601 to 0.0621 on every track, whatever the span, footprint, lookahead, wheel_track or wheel_radius (iteration 4 moved oval only from 0.0614 to 0.0601). Iteration 3 matched iteration 2 exactly, so ki 0.05 vs 0.5 and wheel_track 0.10 vs 0.12 did not move the floor. Line losses are fixed by a span of ±0.05 or wider (iterations 2 and 4). Slalom progress was 0.110 at ±0.04 (with line losses) and 0.035 at ±0.05 and ±0.06 (without). What I had to do in the controller: I kept the iteration 4 controller unchanged, so the mass test is not confounded. Lower mass reduces yaw inertia, so the robot may turn faster; kd 0.15 is kept to damp that. Next race: if max_error on oval and s-bend falls below about 0.058 with line_loss_events still 0, keep mass 0.6 and try 0.4 kg next. If max_error stays at 0.060 to 0.062 and the response looks unchanged, mass is not the floor, so test wheel_radius 0.04 next. If line_loss_events rise above 0, return mass to 0.8 and restore ±0.05 span tuning.
requested_changes: If max_error on oval and s-bend drops below about 0.058 with mass 0.6 and line_loss_events still 0, keep the span and try mass 0.4 kg, because the mass test is the only untested body lever and lower yaw inertia is the expected cause.

If max_error stays at 0.060 to 0.062 with mass 0.6, the mass floor is ruled out, so try wheel_radius 0.04 with the ±0.05 span, since iteration 4 showed a larger radius moved oval max_error slightly (0.0614 to 0.0601).

If slalom progress stays at 0.035 with the ±0.05 span, try outer sensors at ±0.045 with 16 mm footprints, because the ±0.04 span reached slalom progress 0.110 in iteration 1 but with line losses, so a span between ±0.04 and ±0.05 may keep both.
